turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through a few important questions to ensure your safety and comfort during the procedure. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, of course. I'm ready.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Let's start with your medical history. Can you briefly tell me about the reason for your surgery today?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I've been having a lot of pain in my abdomen, especially after eating. The doctor found stones in my gallbladder, so they're removing it laparoscopically.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Now, regarding your medications, I see from your records that you're on Metformin, Gliclazide, Atorvastatin, and you've stopped Ranitidine. Can you please confirm if there have been any changes to your medication list since your last review?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Actually, yes. I stopped taking Gliclazide a few months ago because I was having too many low sugar episodes. My doctor switched me to Sitagliptin 100mg once daily instead.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for letting me know. It's important we have the most up-to-date information. Have you experienced any new allergic reactions to medications recently?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh, yes. I had an allergic reaction to Ceftriaxone last year. I got hives all over my body, so I shouldn't have that antibiotic again.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. We'll make sure to note that in your chart. Your allergies were previously listed as only Penicillin with a rash. This is an important update.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I should have mentioned it earlier, but it slipped my mind.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: No worries at all. That's why we do this interview — to catch any updates. Now, regarding your diabetes, how well-controlled is it on your current medications?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: It's been pretty good since I switched to Sitagliptin. My fasting sugar is usually around 120-140, and I don't have as many spikes as before.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. And how about your weight and mobility? You're listed as having a BMI of 32. How do you feel about your overall fitness level?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I know I'm overweight, but I can still walk and do daily activities without too much trouble. I just get tired faster than before.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's helpful to know. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, this is my first time. I'm a bit nervous, but I trust the team.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's completely normal. We're here to make sure everything goes smoothly. Finally, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I've been fasting as instructed. Just a sip of water with my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect. Thank you so much for going through all that with me. I'll be using general anesthesia for your surgery, and we'll also be doing a Transversus Abdominis Plane block under ultrasound guidance to help with your pain after surgery. Any questions for me before we proceed?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.
